chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: December 1938 Victor session with songs from her films
summary: Titles of the session, with 'Kind of Lonesome' from the film and 'It Ain't Necessarily So'.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: You had one more recording session in New York before you actually went out to Hollywood. And that was on the 10th of December.
Yes.
For Victor again.
Yes.
Four titles: 'Night And Day,' 'Kind Of Lonesome,' 'It Ain't Necessarily So,' and 'Say It With A Kiss.'
Yes.
Okay. Two of these songs from December of 38 were from the movies that you made that year.

Yes. 'Kind Of Lonesome' is from St. Louis Blues. I think I mentioned before that after they padded my part in the movie, Hoagy Carmichael wrote 'Kind Of Lonesome', and there was a scene that sort of linked some of the bigger scenes together in which I sang 'Kind Of Lonesome' with Nat King Cole still in the background.
Unfortunately, there's no

78 of that record at the Institute of Jazz Studies.
Really?
I regret to say it, I haven't heard it yet.
Well, I had it at one time, but I'm sure I don't have it now. I lost a lot of my recordings.
'It Ain't Necessarily So' -- we did that because at the time 'Porgy and Bess' was on Broadway -- the version of it was on Broadway, and so we did that.
Say It with A Kiss was from the other movie that I made out in Hollywood. The one with Dick Powell and Anita Louise.
But it was cut out --
And Louis Armstrong.
And Louis Armstrong.
In fact, Dick Powell -- everybody sang a chorus of it. Dick Powell sang a chorus of it, Anita louise sang a chorus of it, Louis sang a chorus of it, and I sang a chorus of it.
And they cut the whole thing out of the
